title: Weather and zero-shot forecasting models: backtest results for GB electricity demand (part 1 of 2)
note: KEPT as gb-demand-weather-zero-shot-backtest. In a preregistered 960-day day-ahead backtest on GB national demand, identical honestly timed weather forecasts cut error for Chronos-2, Timestral-209M, TimesFM 2.5 and a weekly-lag regression, and the models' lead over the regression mostly vanishes once the regression has weather. Query: feed:zenodo

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty
note: KEPT as tsfm-load-covariate-uncertainty. On three load datasets Chronos-2 is the most accurate zero-shot and fine-tuned when future covariates are known or well forecast, but it degrades as covariate forecasts get noisier, where TimesNet holds up better. Query: feed:arxiv

title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer
note: KEPT as pjm-cold-spell-calibration-benchmark. In a pre-registered benchmark over four PJM extreme-cold events, 90% load-forecast intervals lose coverage inside the events and no conformal calibrator chosen without the target event restores it; leave-one-event-out evaluation overstates coverage against chronological evaluation. Query: feed:zenodo

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model
note: KEPT as chronos2-covariate-grid-load. On ISO New England and ENTSO-E load, Chronos-2 with covariates gains substantially from task-specific fine-tuning and is strong at short horizons against task-specific deep learning models. Query: feed:arxiv

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets
note: KEPT as foretec-energybench. A live daily benchmark that runs eighteen foundation models, linear and boosted models and operator forecasts on one frozen information set for six European zones; over the first 32 live days weather covariates lowered the error of every foundation model run with and without them. Query: feed:arxiv

title: Timestral
note: KEPT as timestral. Mistral's four open-weight forecasting models (5M to 209M parameters) are reported to lead GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench among zero-shot models and accept known-future covariates. Query: time series foundation model release

title: TimesFM 3.0
note: KEPT as timesfm-3. Google's 330M-parameter TimesFM 3.0 forecasts multivariate series zero-shot with past and known-future covariates and is reported top among pretrained models on GIFT-Eval, fev-bench and TIME; the weights carry a non-commercial licence. Query: feed:huggingface

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context
note: KEPT as t0-forecasting-with-context. The open-weight t0 models condition on past and known-future covariates without retraining; known-future covariates raise t0-alpha's skill by about six points over 30 tasks, and the later t0-gamma card reports gains over t0-beta on every listed benchmark. Query: feed:arxiv

title: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of TimesFM 3 on Post-Release, Multivariate and Controlled Data
note: KEPT as timesfm3-leakage-aware-evaluation. Under a protocol frozen before the test data existed, TimesFM 3 beats a pre-specified classical ensemble on post-release data including electricity load, but in two prospective weeks its point-forecast lead on load is not confirmed and its 80% intervals cover about 70%. Query: feed:zenodo

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels: Time-Series Transformers Outperform Established Methods
note: KEPT as load-benchmark-across-grid-levels. Across a control area, low-voltage feeders and end consumers, Transformer forecasters cut short-term load error by roughly 7 to 11% against established methods, and zero-shot Chronos-2 is competitive on two datasets but misses special events on the control-area data. Query: feed:arxiv

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models for Adaptive Probabilistic Electricity Load Forecasting
note: KEPT as weather-forecast-aggregation-gam-load. For French national load, an adaptive additive model fed several weather-forecast providers at once beats single-provider versions, most clearly for probabilistic forecasts and extreme quantiles. Query: feed:arxiv

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
note: KEPT as peft-tsfm-electrical-load. Across four load aggregation levels pretrained Moirai and Chronos-2 beat seasonal naive and XGBoost baselines, and rank-16 LoRA on Moirai Large cuts normalised MAE by about 7.5% while updating about 1% of the weights. Query: feed:arxiv

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
note: KEPT as peak-aware-stlf-aggregation-levels. On UK and Swiss distribution data Chronos-2 has the lowest high-demand-period error at every aggregation level, 20 to 51% below LightGBM and XGBoost. Query: feed:arxiv

title: pl-forecast-bench: a leakage-checked forecasting benchmark for the Polish power system
note: KEPT as pl-forecast-bench. A benchmark that fixes data, as-of rules for every input, a 12-month test year and reference models (naive, operator plan, ridge, boosting, zero-shot foundation models) for Polish demand, wind, solar and price, with tests that detect look-ahead. Query: feed:zenodo

title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 for Zero-Shot Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks
note: KEPT as tabpfn-ts-chronos2-heat-load. For hourly 24-hour heat-load forecasts in two German networks, zero-shot TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 with ambient temperature beat every trained baseline on point accuracy over a full year; the main benchmark assumes perfect weather, with a separate forecast-weather sensitivity run. Query: feed:arxiv

title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
note: KEPT as timesfm3-university-building-day-ahead. On 57 test days for one building TimesFM 3.0 with covariates has the lowest error, about 43% below weekly seasonal naive, but paired comparisons do not separate it from XGBoost, and covariates help only on holidays. Query: feed:arxiv

title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine
note: KEPT as tsfm-vs-khepri-carbon-intensity-prereg. In a preregistered comparison, univariate Timestral and Chronos-2 have lower MAPE than SARIMA and boosted baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts on a 2025 test year, while a 14-origin post-release holdout is within the minimum detectable effect and reported as undetermined. Query: feed:arxiv

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data
note: KEPT as point-in-time-leakage-electricity-data. Choosing the latest weather-model run issued before an auction gate picks a run that was not yet published on over 99% of days for six of ten configurations in Great Britain, with an apparent accuracy effect between -9% and +24%. Query: feed:arxiv

title: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
note: KEPT as calendar-encoding-covariate-tsfm. Across four covariate-aware foundation models and nine calendar-driven datasets, the choice among seven calendar encodings changes zero-shot MASE by up to about 10% on ordinary days and far more on holidays. Query: feed:arxiv

title: Multi-horizon forecasting of national electricity demand in Türkiye: run records, forecasts and trained models
note: KEPT as turkiye-national-demand-multi-horizon. An archive of 759 training runs with sealed test forecasts for national demand at several horizons using calendar, holiday and temperature inputs; the record itself states no headline number. Query: feed:zenodo

title: Closed-Form Calendar Estimation in Deep Load Forecasting: An Information-Controlled Benchmark on Eight National Grids
note: KEPT as closed-form-calendar-deep-load. Companion archive of per-window errors and probabilistic runs for a benchmark of deep load forecasters on eight national grids that controls what calendar information each model gets; the record states no headline number. Query: feed:zenodo

title: TimeH2O-v1
note: KEPT as timeh2o-v1. H2O.ai's 108M-parameter model takes a target with optional covariates and its card reports leading zero-shot scores on GIFT-Eval and fev-bench; weights are gated under a non-commercial licence, with paper and code not yet out. Query: feed:huggingface

title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
note: KEPT as timer-m1. A pretrained multivariate model trained on synthesised episodes with target, past-only and known-future covariate roles is reported first on fev-bench and TIME and second on GIFT-Eval. Query: feed:arxiv

title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Mode
note: KEPT as causal-audit-covariate-tsfm-prereg. On a preregistered grid with exact counterfactuals, Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM 2.5 respond to a future covariate path associationally and more confounded than a regression does. Query: feed:arxiv

title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out
note: KEPT as pretraining-familiarity-post-release-holdout. On data published after every tested model was released, pretrained forecasters win five of seven groups, and their advantage tracks how familiar the domain is from pretraining rather than seasonality. Query: feed:arxiv

title: Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
note: KEPT as timesfm3-vs-classical-simulation. On 7,200 simulated series under a pre-registered protocol neither TimesFM-3 nor classical methods dominate: TimesFM-3 is never far from the best method, while automatic ARIMA is 21 to 24% better on seasonal data with four or more cycles. Query: feed:arxiv

title: Tabby: An Open Pretraining Recipe for Time Series Foundation Models
note: KEPT as tabby-open-pretraining-recipe. A 145M-parameter open model with contexts up to 8,192 points and a published training recipe is reported competitive zero-shot on GIFT-Eval and TIME. Query: feed:arxiv

title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
note: KEPT as pathfm. A flow-matching model that generates whole future paths, distilled to one or two steps, is reported competitive on fev-bench and TIME and best on a new path-score benchmark that scores peak load and cumulative demand. Query: feed:arxiv

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model
note: KEPT as medium-term-load-economic-covariates. For French load forecast 1 to 48 months ahead with a tabular foundation model, selected economic covariates improve skill by about 20% over 2015 to 2025. Query: feed:arxiv

title: U.S. utility load forecasts filed on FERC Form 714, 2006-2025: forecast errors, weather-normalized outcomes, prediction
note: KEPT as ferc-714-load-forecast-errors. Code and data scoring about 13,700 filed peak and energy forecasts from US balancing authorities, PJM's own included, against weather-normalised outcomes, with intervals built from past errors. Query: feed:zenodo

title: PatchTST-FM-r2 (IBM Granite)
note: KEPT as patchtst-fm-r2. IBM's 385M-parameter zero-shot model is described on its card as the top GIFT-Eval model under a permissive commercial-friendly licence. Query: feed:huggingface

title: Tafsut Univariate Base
note: KEPT as tafsut-univariate-base. A 105M-parameter MIT-licensed univariate model whose card places it third on CRPS and fourth on MASE among twelve models on GIFT-Eval. Query: feed:huggingface

title: gridload-compact
note: KEPT as gridload-compact. Two small quantile networks (about 160k parameters) trained on German net-load history are self-scored on the TS-Arena archive as ahead of the best reference model at 24 hours and tied with Chronos-2 at 72 hours; the card says its own pre-registered live go/no-go rule failed. Query: feed:huggingface

title: Thaki EnergyLoad Forecaster v0.1
note: KEPT as thaki-energyload-forecaster. Three LightGBM models for per-meter load at 15 minutes, 1 hour and 24 hours on the public UCI Portuguese dataset beat persistence and seasonal naive on MASE on a 2014 test half-year. Query: feed:huggingface

title: A controlled benchmark of temporal dependence for day-ahead electricity-demand discrepancies in Great Britain
note: KEPT as gb-demand-discrepancy-dependence-benchmark. A retrospective benchmark on 364 days of 2024 comparing independent, Gaussian-copula and empirical ensembles of day-ahead demand forecast discrepancies, keeping adverse and inconclusive findings. Query: feed:zenodo

title: Türkiye Grid Foundation Model
note: KEPT as turkiye-grid-foundation-model. Research software for studying transfer across electricity consumption, renewable generation and day-ahead price in Türkiye with chronological evaluation; the record states no result. Query: feed:zenodo

title: Zero-shot time series foundation models for statistical postprocessing of weather forecasts: how much training data do t
note: KEPT as tsfm-weather-postprocessing. Code release for a comparison of zero-shot TimesFM-3 and Chronos-2, given the ensemble mean as a covariate, with trained statistical postprocessing of 2 m temperature forecasts at 49 German stations. Query: time series foundation model release

title: BQEB ForecastBench: Benchmarking AI Models for Smart Grid Forecasting Using BQEB-Data v1
note: KEPT as bqeb-forecastbench. An open benchmark for next-hour load and day-ahead price forecasting that scores linear regression, random forest and gradient boosting under one chronological split. Query: feed:zenodo
